children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange erased earlier losses on Thursday before showing independent strength.
Crude oil prices were down after reports of Saudi crude cargoes moving through Oman. Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were lower.

The canola market shifted its focus away from Statistics Canada's satellite imagery-based principal field crop report released on Wednesday, which projected the 2026-27 crop at 22.1 million tonnes. An analyst expects lower figures in the December survey-based report.
The Saskatchewan crop report said the province's canola harvest was 15 per cent complete as of Sept. 14. That compares with 21 per cent at the same point a year ago as wet conditions cause delays.
At mid-afternoon, the Canadian dollar was down two-tenths of a U.S. cent compared to Wednesday's close.
There were 49,230 canola contracts traded on Thursday, compared to Wednesday when 61,399 contracts changed hands. Spreads accounted for 28,070 contracts in today's trade.
Settlement prices are in Canadian dollars per metric tonne.
